bibl.title: Chiaroscuro. Oltre l’angolo di scrittura (secoli I a.C. – VI d.C.)
bibl.note: After a critical review of past contributions about the writing angle in Greco-Roman times, the authors study the relationship between the latter and the contrast between thick and thin strokes (the so-called "chiaroscuro") in the rustic capital and in the uncial. In both scriptures, variations in the "chiaroscuro" show that this was related to aesthetic and not rigidly regulated by a predetermined and stable writing angle. bibl.seg: Guglielmo Cavallo & Paolo Fioretti, Chiaroscuro. Oltre l'angolo di scrittura (secoli I a.C. - VI d.C.).

After a critical review of past contributions about the writing angle in Greco-Roman times, the authors study the relationship between the latter and the contrast between thick and thin strokes (the so-called "chiaroscuro") in the rustic capital and in the uncial. In both scriptures, variations in the "chiaroscuro" show that this was related to aesthetic and not rigidly regulated by a predetermined and stable writing angle. The prevalence of a "chiaroscuro" oblique or vertical perhaps depends on graphic trends that belong to different areas of production, and certainly not to different periods; also sometimes it is possible to observe reciprocal influences between Latin and Greek writing.
